messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Kai, a 53-year-old photographer from Oceania, sat in his dimly lit studio, surrounded by the familiar comfort of cameras and editing equipment. Yet, despite this sanctuary, his body remained tense, perpetually on guard against potential dangers that lurked outside these walls. This constant state of alertness was a stark contrast to the calm, creative energy he once embodied behind the lens. Kai's life took a drastic turn three years ago when he was held captive by an armed group while on assignment in a conflict zone. The memories of those harrowing days still lingered vividly – the sound of footsteps outside his makeshift cell, the feel of cold metal against his skin, and the smell of stale air that seemed to suffocate him. Since then, Kai's world had shrunk significantly, with every new environment presenting a potential threat. When entering any space, whether it was a bustling coffee shop or an empty park, Kai's instincts compelled him to scan for escape routes and identify safe seats – positions where he could observe his surroundings without being caught off guard. This hypervigilance towards people also led him to notice the smallest details: a twitch in someone's hand, a hesitation before speaking, or the way their eyes seemed to linger on him for just a fraction too long. Kai had come to believe that these precautions were necessary to ensure his survival, but they also left him feeling constantly on edge. His body remained tense and ready to react at all times, as if waiting for the next sudden movement or unexpected noise would send him spiraling back into captivity. To cope with this ever-present threat, Kai found himself seeking reassurance from those around him – friends, family, even strangers in passing conversations. He'd ask them if they thought he was being paranoid, if his fears were justified, and if they believed he was truly safe. However, each reassurance only provided temporary relief, as the seeds of doubt had already taken root. Kai began to plan escape routes before entering any new environment – mentally mapping exits, identifying potential hiding spots, and anticipating worst-case scenarios. This obsessive planning reinforced his perception of danger lurking around every corner, fueling a vicious cycle that threatened to consume him. As the weeks turned into months, Kai noticed changes in how he interacted with others. His once-vibrant relationships began to suffer as friends and family grew tired of his constant questions and anxious demeanor. Even his work suffered – clients found his erratic behavior unsettling, and his usual creative spark was all but extinguished by the all-consuming fear. Kai's wife, Leilani, tried her best to be supportive, but even she couldn't understand why he insisted on sitting in certain chairs or why he'd freeze at sudden noises. She felt helpless as she watched the man she loved become increasingly isolated and withdrawn. The tension between them grew thicker than the air in Kai's makeshift cell all those years ago. It was this realization that finally brought Kai to seek help – a glimmer of hope that there might be a way to break free from this suffocating cycle of fear and reclaim his life, his relationships, and his passion for photography. As he sat in the dimly lit studio, surrounded by the shadows of his past, Kai knew it was time to confront the darkness head-on, no matter how daunting the task seemed.
